attempts.summary: Published node2's HTTP service (port 8080) on node1's (OPNsense) management address, port 80, via a pf DNAT (rdr) rule plus a hairpin SNAT rule so return traffic routes back correctly. Filter rules restrict access to source node3 only; every other source (node2 itself, node1 itself) gets an immediate TCP RST (connection refused), not a timeout. Also had to stand up the HTTP service on node2 (it did not pre-exist) as a systemd unit, and locked node2's own firewalld down to accept 8080 only from node1. All three nodes were sequentially restarted with verified boot-identity changes and confirmed post-restart recovery of config, services, and the access-control behavior.
